Weighted: for every real s, bounded coefficientwise convergence implies WeakDual(WeightedCoeff (sobolev (-s)) 1) convergence with physical index reversal.
Weighted: finite truncations converge weak-star at infinity for every real s.
Original periodic distributions: bounded modewise convergence implies actual Wiener-predual weak-star convergence via existing pseudomeasureDualIsometry.
All real predual orders r: entire weighted endpoint norm balls are weak-star compact, metrizable and sequentially compact. Parameter r denotes predual order; source coefficient order is s=-r.
Every bounded subset has exactly its coordinate-induced topology, expressed as an actual topological embedding; criterion holds for arbitrary filters.
Arbitrary sets in this weak dual are compact iff sequentially compact iff norm-bounded and weak-star closed; sequential compactness implies boundedness by Banach-Steinhaus.
Weak-star convergence of sequences is equivalent to boundedness plus coefficient convergence; boundedness is derived in the forward direction.
For every finite ENNReal exponent p with Fact(1<=p), at (-r-t)*p.toReal>1, the lower norm realization preserves raw coefficients and induces exactly the weak-star topology on bounded sets.
Weak-star sequence convergence is equivalent to boundedness plus lower weighted norm convergence at every admissible pair (t,p).
A set is weak-star compact iff norm bounded and its actual lower weighted norm image is compact.
Real conjugate-symmetric mean-zero coefficients form a closed subset; its intersections with weighted norm balls are compact, metrizable and sequentially compact.
